$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.21,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.21/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and 7ce581172c3fd0c78e9d583b2ef0e38ae1595c16318f31b66d50e8a972a002ad and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.21/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
7ce581172c3fd0c78e9d583b2ef0e38ae1595c16318f31b66d50e8a972a002ad is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
